Claude responded: The command ran successfully!

The command ran successfully! Here's what happened:

✓ Launcher icons were generated successfully. A couple of things worth noting from the output:

Deprecation warning — you used flutter pub run but the newer way is:

bash
dart run flutter_launcher_icons

Deprecated config key — in your pubspec.yaml or flutter_launcher_icons.yaml, you're using flutter_icons: as the key. Rename it to flutter_launcher_icons: to fix that warning.

iOS alpha channel warning — if you're targeting the App Store, add this to your config to avoid rejection:

yaml
flutter_launcher_icons:
  remove_alpha_ios: true

"No platform provided" message — this is informational, not an error. It just means you didn't specify a platform flag (like --ios or --android), so it defaulted to generating for all configured platforms.

Everything looks good overall — your launcher icons have been generated and should now be applied to your app!

Claude responded: Run this command to generate icons only for Android:

Run this command to generate icons only for Android:

bash
dart run flutter_launcher_icons -f flutter_launcher_icons.yaml --flavor android

Or the simpler way:

bash

The -p android flag targets Android only, skipping iOS entirely. This should eliminate the alpha channel warning as well since that's iOS-specific.

Claude responded: The error means it can't find the launcher icons configuration.

The error means it can't find the launcher icons configuration. Let's fix it.

Check your pubspec.yaml — make sure you have this section (with the correct key):

yaml
flutter_launcher_icons:
  android: true
  ios: false
  image_path: "assets/icons/app_icon.png"  # update this to your actual icon path

⚠️ If you previously used flutter_icons: as the key, rename it to flutter_launcher_icons:

Or create a separate flutter_launcher_icons.yaml file in your project root:

yaml
flutter_launcher_icons:
  android: true
  ios: false
  image_path: "assets/icons/app_icon.png"  # update to your actual icon path

Then run:

bash
dart run flutter_launcher_icons

If your config file has a different name, point to it explicitly:

bash
dart run flutter_launcher_icons --file flutter_launcher_icons.yaml

GitHub will show you these commands after creating — run them in your project folder:

bash

git push -u origin main

Replace YOUR_USERNAME with your actual GitHub username.

Let me know once you've created the repo on GitHub and I'll help you with any errors that come up!

Claude responded: Both folders (taxiappbackend and taxiappfrontend) are showing as blue folder icons with a small arrow — that means they were pushed as submodules, not as regul…

Both folders (taxi_app_backend and taxi_app_frontend) are showing as blue folder icons with a small arrow — that means they were pushed as submodules, not as regular folders. That's why you can't open them!

Let's fix this by removing them as submodules and re-adding as normal folders.

Step 1 — Remove the cached submodule references:

bash
git rm --cached taxi_app_backend
git rm --cached taxi_app_frontend

Step 2 — Delete the .git folder inside each subfolder (this is what caused the submodule issue):

bash
rm -rf FinalYearProject/taxi_app_backend/.git
rm -rf FinalYearProject/taxi_app_frontend/.git

Step 3 — Re-add everything as normal files:

bash
git add .
git commit -m "Fix: re-add folders as regular directories"
git push origin main

After this, the folders on GitHub should show as normal clickable folders and you'll be able to browse the files inside them.

⚠️ Make sure you run these commands from the correct directory. Run pwd first to confirm where you are before running anything.

Claude responded: GitHub blocked your push because it detected a secret/credential file in your repo.

GitHub blocked your push because it detected a secret/credential file in your repo. This is actually good — it's protecting you!

The file taxi_app_backend/storage/firebase-adminsdk.json contains your Google Cloud Service Account key which should never be public.

Step 1 — Add the file to .gitignore immediately:

bash
echo "taxi_app_backend/storage/firebase-adminsdk.json" >> .gitignore

Step 2 — Remove it from git tracking:

bash
git rm --cached taxi_app_backend/storage/firebase-adminsdk.json

Step 3 — Remove it from git history too (important!):

bash
git filter-branch --force --index-filter "git rm --cached --ignore-unmatch taxi_app_backend/storage/firebase-adminsdk.json" --prune-empty --tag-name-filter cat -- --all

Step 4 — Force push:

bash
git push origin main --force

⚠️ IMPORTANT SECURITY STEPS:

  • Go to Google Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Service Accounts
  • Delete or revoke that service account key immediately
  • Generate a new key and store it locally only, never commit it
  • Add *.json or specifically firebase-adminsdk.json to your .gitignore for all future projects

Claude responded: Same firebase-adminsdk.

Same firebase-adminsdk.json problem again! Let's fix it properly this time before pushing.

Step 1 — Add the file to .gitignore:

bash
echo "storage/firebase-adminsdk.json" >> .gitignore

Step 2 — Remove it from git tracking:

bash
git rm --cached storage/firebase-adminsdk.json

Step 3 — Remove git history and start fresh:

bash
rm -rf .git
git init
git branch -M main

Step 4 — Add, commit and push:

bash
git add .
git commit -m "Initial commit - backend"
git remote add origin https://github.com/TshewangC26/Taxi_App_Backend_V2.git
git push -u origin main

This time it will work because:

  • The .gitignore now excludes firebase-adminsdk.json
  • We wiped the git history so the secret is no longer in any old commit
  • We're pushing a clean fresh history

Claude responded: No changes needed to your local .

No changes needed to your local .env file!

Here's why:

  • Your local .env is only used when running the app on your computer for development
  • Railway has its own separate environment variables that override everything when deployed
  • The .env file is also in .gitignore so it never gets pushed to GitHub

The only thing you need to update locally is APP_URL once your Railway deployment is working:

dotenv
# Keep this for local development
APP_URL=http://localhost

# You'll use this Railway URL in your Flutter app later
# https://your-app-name.railway.app

The flow is:

Local development  → uses .env file (localhost)
Railway production → uses Railway Variables (live URL)
Flutter app        → will point to Railway URL

So your local .env stays as is. Focus on getting Railway deployment working first, then we'll update the Flutter app's API URL to point to the live Railway backend.

Two problems:

  1. It's still using the private internal host instead of your public one
  2. PHP PostgreSQL driver (pdo_pgsql) is not installed on the Railway PHP image

Fix 1 — Add a nixpacks.toml file in your taxi_app_backend root to install the pgsql driver:

bash
cd ~/OneDrive/desktop/FinalYearProject/taxi_app_backend

Create a file called nixpacks.toml with this content:

toml
[phases.setup]
nixPkgs = ["php83", "php83Extensions.pdo_pgsql", "php83Extensions.pgsql"]

[start]
cmd = "php artisan migrate --force && php artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=$PORT"

Fix 2 — Push the file to GitHub:

bash
git add nixpacks.toml
git commit -m "Add nixpacks config for pgsql driver"
git push origin main

Fix 3 — Update DB_HOST in Railway Backend variables:

DB_HOST=turntable.proxy.rlwy.net
DB_PORT=44725

Make sure it's NOT postgres.railway.internal anymore.

Claude responded: Great news!

Great news! This is actually progress — it connected to PostgreSQL successfully! 🎉

The error relation "bookings" already exists means migrations ran before and the tables already exist. Just update your nixpacks.toml to use migrate --force with a skip existing flag:

Update nixpacks.toml in your taxi_app_backend folder:

toml
[phases.setup]
nixPkgs = ["php83", "php83Extensions.pdo_pgsql", "php83Extensions.pgsql"]

[start]
cmd = "php artisan migrate --force --skip-existing 2>/dev/null || true && php artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=$PORT"

Or even simpler — just ignore migration errors and start the server:

toml
[phases.setup]
nixPkgs = ["php83", "php83Extensions.pdo_pgsql", "php83Extensions.pgsql"]

[start]
cmd = "php artisan migrate --force 2>/dev/null; php artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=$PORT"

Then push:

bash
git add nixpacks.toml
git commit -m "Fix migration error on redeploy"
git push origin main

After this deploys, check if your Railway URL is live by visiting it in the browser — it should show the Laravel welcome page!

Claude responded: The migration is still failing because the tables already exist from a previous run.

The migration is still failing because the tables already exist from a previous run. The 2>/dev/null fix didn't work because Laravel throws an exception before the server starts.

Let's fix this properly by updating nixpacks.toml to use migrate --force only if needed:

Update your nixpacks.toml:

toml
[phases.setup]
nixPkgs = ["php83", "php83Extensions.pdo_pgsql", "php83Extensions.pgsql", "php83Extensions.mbstring", "php83Extensions.xml", "php83Extensions.curl", "php83Extensions.tokenizer", "php83Extensions.ctype", "php83Extensions.fileinfo", "php83Extensions.bcmath"]

[phases.install]
cmds = ["composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader"]

[phases.build]
cmds = ["php artisan config:cache", "php artisan route:cache", "php artisan view:cache"]

[start]
cmd = "php artisan migrate:status 2>/dev/null; php artisan migrate --force --pretend 2>/dev/null; php artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=$PORT"

Actually the simplest fix — just drop and recreate the database tables. Since this is a fresh deployment run this in Railway:

  • Go to Postgres service → Connect tab → copy the psql command
  • Or update nixpacks.toml start command to:
toml
[start]
cmd = "php artisan migrate:fresh --force 2>/dev/null || php artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=$PORT && php artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=$PORT"

Then push:

bash
git add nixpacks.toml
git commit -m "Fix: use migrate fresh to avoid duplicate table errors"

First update your API base URL in Flutter to point to your Railway backend.

Step 1 — Find your Railway backend URL:

  • Go to Railway → Taxi_App_Backend_V2 → Settings tab
  • Look for Domains section — it looks like https://taxi-app-backend-v2.railway.app

Step 2 — Update the API URL in your Flutter project:

  • Find the file where your base URL is defined (likely in lib/ folder)
  • Run this to find it:
bash
cd ~/OneDrive/desktop/FinalYearProject/taxi_app_frontend
grep -r "localhost" lib/

This will show which files have localhost so you can update them.

Step 3 — Replace localhost with your Railway URL:

dart
// Change from:

7 May

Claude responded: Here's the fully updated api_service.

Here's the fully updated api_service.dart:

dart
import 'dart:convert';
import 'dart:io';
import 'package:http/http.dart' as http;
import 'package:shared_preferences/shared_preferences.dart';

class ApiService {
  static const String baseUrl = 'https://taxiappbackendv2-kspb-production.up.railway.app/api';

  Future<String?> getToken() async {
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    return prefs.getString('auth_token');
  }

  Future<void> saveToken(String token) async {
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.setString('auth_token', token);
  }

  Future<void> removeToken() async {
    final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance();
    await prefs.remove('auth_token');
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> get(String endpoint) async {
    final token = await getToken();
    final response = await http.get(
      Uri.parse('$baseUrl$endpoint'),
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
        if (token != null) 'Authorization': 'Bearer $token',
      },
    );
    return _handleResponse(response);
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> post(
      String endpoint, Map<String, dynamic> data) async {
    final token = await getToken();
    final response = await http.post(
      Uri.parse('$baseUrl$endpoint'),
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
        if (token != null) 'Authorization': 'Bearer $token',
      },
      body: jsonEncode(data),
    );
    return _handleResponse(response);
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> put(
      String endpoint, Map<String, dynamic> data) async {
    final token = await getToken();
    final response = await http.put(
      Uri.parse('$baseUrl$endpoint'),
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
        if (token != null) 'Authorization': 'Bearer $token',
      },
      body: jsonEncode(data),
    );
    return _handleResponse(response);
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> delete(String endpoint) async {
    final token = await getToken();
    final response = await http.delete(
      Uri.parse('$baseUrl$endpoint'),
      headers: {
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Accept': 'application/json',
        if (token != null) 'Authorization': 'Bearer $token',
      },
    );
    return _handleResponse(response);
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> updateProfile({
    required String name,
    required String phone,
    String? imagePath,
  }) async {
    final token = await getToken();

    final request = http.MultipartRequest(
      'POST',
      Uri.parse('$baseUrl/profile/update'),
    );

    request.headers.addAll({
      'Accept': 'application/json',
      if (token != null) 'Authorization': 'Bearer $token',
    });

    request.fields['name']  = name;
    request.fields['phone'] = phone;

    if (imagePath != null) {
      request.files.add(
        await http.MultipartFile.fromPath('profile_photo', imagePath),
      );
    }

    final streamedResponse = await request.send();
    final response = await http.Response.fromStream(streamedResponse);

    return _handleResponse(response);
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> postMultipart(
    String endpoint, {
    required Map<String, String> fields,
    String? fileField,
    String? filePath,
  }) async {
    final token = await getToken();

    final request = http.MultipartRequest(
      'POST',
      Uri.parse('$baseUrl$endpoint'),
    );

    request.headers.addAll({
      'Accept': 'application/json',
      if (token != null) 'Authorization': 'Bearer $token',
    });

    request.fields.addAll(fields);

    if (fileField != null && filePath != null) {
      request.files.add(
        await http.MultipartFile.fromPath(fileField, filePath),
      );
    }

    final streamedResponse = await request.send();
    final response = await http.Response.fromStream(streamedResponse);

    return _handleResponse(response);
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> getDriverPaymentDetails(int bookingId) async {
    return await get('/driver/payment-details/$bookingId');
  }

  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> createPayment({
    required int bookingId,
    required String paymentMethod,
    String? transactionId,
    String? screenshotPath,
    String? notes,
  }) async {
    final token = await getToken();

    final request = http.MultipartRequest(
      'POST',
      Uri.parse('$baseUrl/payments'),
    );

    request.headers.addAll({
      'Accept': 'application/json',
      if (token != null) 'Authorization': 'Bearer $token',
    });

    request.fields['booking_id']     = bookingId.toString();
    request.fields['payment_method'] = paymentMethod;
    if (transactionId != null)
      request.fields['transaction_id'] = transactionId;
    if (notes != null) request.fields['notes'] = notes;

    if (screenshotPath != null) {
      request.files.add(
        await http.MultipartFile.fromPath('screenshot', screenshotPath),
      );
    }

    final streamedResponse = await request.send();
    final response = await http.Response.fromStream(streamedResponse);

    return _handleResponse(response);
  }

  Map<String, dynamic> _handleResponse(http.Response response) {
    if (response.statusCode >= 200 && response.statusCode < 300) {
      return jsonDecode(response.body);
    } else {
      throw Exception('API Error: ${response.body}');
    }
  }
}

flutter build apk --release

Claude responded: The issue is a PNG file in the wrong folder.

The issue is a PNG file in the wrong folder. Fix it by moving the file:

bash
cd ~/OneDrive/desktop/FinalYearProject/taxi_app_frontend
mv android/app/src/main/res/android_icons/store_icon.png android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-xxxhdpi/store_icon.png

The android_icons folder should not be inside res/ — that folder only accepts .xml files. The launcher icons generated by flutter_launcher_icons should already be in the correct mipmap-* folders.

Claude responded: The error is Maximum execution time of 30 seconds exceeded — the SMTP connection is timing out.

The error is Maximum execution time of 30 seconds exceeded — the SMTP connection is timing out. This means Railway is blocking outgoing SMTP connections on port 465.

Fix — Switch to port 587 with TLS instead of 465 with SSL.

Step 1 — Update Railway Variables:

MAIL_PORT=587
MAIL_ENCRYPTION=tls

Step 2 — Update config/mail.php defaults:

php
'smtp' => [
    'transport' => 'smtp',
    'host' => env('MAIL_HOST', 'smtp.gmail.com'),
    'port' => env('MAIL_PORT', 587),
    'encryption' => env('MAIL_ENCRYPTION', 'tls'),
    'username' => env('MAIL_USERNAME'),
    'password' => env('MAIL_PASSWORD'),
    'timeout' => 60,
],

Step 3 — Also increase PHP max execution time in nixpacks.toml:

toml
[phases.setup]
nixPkgs = ["php83", "php83Extensions.pdo_pgsql", "php83Extensions.pgsql", "php83Extensions.mbstring", "php83Extensions.xml", "php83Extensions.curl", "php83Extensions.tokenizer", "php83Extensions.ctype", "php83Extensions.fileinfo", "php83Extensions.bcmath"]

[phases.install]
cmds = ["composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader"]

[phases.build]
cmds = ["php artisan config:clear", "php artisan config:cache", "php artisan route:cache", "php artisan view:cache"]

[start]
cmd = "php artisan migrate --force 2>/dev/null; php -d max_execution_time=120 artisan serve --host=0.0.0.0 --port=$PORT"

Step 4 — Push:

bash
git add config/mail.php nixpacks.toml
git commit -m "Fix SMTP timeout - switch to port 587 tls"
git push origin main

Then test forgot password again!
